prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: Русский / Tiếng Việt · Diacritics (language ru).
Grid: 3 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "Термин" · longest unbreakable unit 152px · widest one-line content 152px
  col 2: header "Tiếng Việt" · longest unbreakable unit 41px · widest one-line content 126px
  col 3: header "Описание" · longest unbreakable unit 101px · widest one-line content 697px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 360px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 360px wide (column widths sum to at most 359px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 360px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"A Russian–Vietnamese reference table pairing technical terms with their equivalents and descriptions.","tasks":["Look up a Russian term and find its Vietnamese equivalent.","Compare the terms and their descriptions across rows.","Read each description to understand the concept."],"relations":["Each row connects a Russian term, its Vietnamese equivalent and a description of the same concept.","The first two columns are parallel labels; the third supplies explanatory context."],"roles":["The first column identifies each concept in Russian.","The second column gives the Vietnamese equivalent.","The third column explains the concept.","The header row labels the three fields."],"keep_whole":["Individual Russian and Vietnamese words, including their diacritics.","Unbreakable units in descriptions."],"may_wrap":["Multiword Vietnamese equivalents may wrap at spaces.","Descriptions may wrap between words.","The Vietnamese column header may wrap between words."],"same_scale":["Cells within each column should share a consistent width and visual role.","The Russian and Vietnamese terms have parallel roles, although their different word lengths require different widths."],"h_vs_v":"The unbreakable content and fixed padding require minimum column widths of 173, 62 and 122 px, totaling 357 px. With at most 359 px available for columns, only 2 px remain to distribute. Descriptions therefore need substantial vertical space, and three substantially different valid width strategies are impossible."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d1r0A.
Measured facts:
d1r0A: column widths [173, 62, 124] px · table 360×541 px · row heights [60, 199, 129, 153] · column headers on >1 line: 1/3 · tallest cell 8 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 360 px viewport (no scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). This is your first look at real renders: propose at least one improved or alternative design (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or test an important idea you have not tried). "done" is not allowed yet. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"best":["your best design name(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"change":"what and why"}]}
